pages.title: From GM crops to genome-edited crops

facts.text: GE rice varieties: improved Samba Mahsuri and MTU-1010; canola-quality low-pungency mustard (2nd year trials, possible release 2026)
facts.head: News

facts.text: ⚠ Only commercial GM crop in India: Bt cotton
facts.head: News

facts.text: Variety: Samba Mahsuri (GE); Edit / benefit: Gn1a (cytokinin oxidase) edited → more spikelets, ~19% yield gain
facts.head: News

facts.text: Variety: MTU-1010 (GE); Edit / benefit: Drought/salt tolerance — saline/alkaline soils
facts.head: News

facts.text: Variety: Mustard (GE); Edit / benefit: Low pungency, disease/pest resistance
facts.head: News

facts.text: March 2022 MoEFCC OM: transgene-free GE plants exempt from GM biosafety rules — need IBSC certification, ⚠ not GEAC
facts.head: Regulation and funding

facts.text: Funding: National Agricultural Science Fund (~2018); ₹500 crore in Union Budget 2023–24
facts.head: Regulation and funding

facts.text: ICAR mapped ~178 genes in 24 field crops and 43 genes in horticultural crops
facts.head: Regulation and funding

facts.text: Cas9, Cas12a; newer GeoCas9, CasLambda supplied by Innovative Genomics Institute (founded by Jennifer Doudna) — training at IARI (Feb 2025)
facts.head: Tools

facts.text: Indigenous TnpB-based mini editor: team led by Kutubuddin Ali Molla, Central Rice Research Institute (CRRI), Cuttack
facts.head: Tools

facts.text: Training: 9 scientists trained abroad (US, Europe, Australia, CIMMYT Mexico); 12 more scheduled
facts.head: Tools

facts.text: GM vs GE: GM inserts foreign genes (transgenic); GE edits own genes, no foreign DNA
facts.head: Tools
